references.text: Pharaoh hardened his heart when the plague ceased, just as Moses had predicted that he and his servants still did not fear the Lord
Pharaoh hardened his heart again and sinned, he and his servants, confirming Moses' words about their lack of fear for God
True fear of the Lord God is a central theme - here Israel is commanded to fear the Lord, in contrast to Pharaoh who did not fear
Fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge - Pharaoh lacked this fear and therefore also true knowledge of God
Even when grace is shown to the wicked, they do not learn righteousness - parallel to Pharaoh who did not fear God despite the signs
The people have eyes but do not see; they do not fear the Lord - the same hardening of heart as with Pharaoh and his servants
Direct narrative connection: 9:17 describes Pharaoh's exaltation, while 9:30 explains that this is due to a lack of fear for God.
Theological parallel: Rom 3:18 generalizes the sinful condition (lack of fear for God) which Pharaoh personified in Exodus.
